title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in July 1986 Grothendieck was building an axiomatics of 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set of elementary objects 𝒜 with data Δ, a disjointness relation | |, and a 'magasin' (store) 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(𝒜) of admissible finite configurations ('figures'). The model case is a 'spatios' Σ. This is a lattice-like structure of spatial elements with Sup ∨, Inf ∧, a complementation ∁ and a disjointness relation e|e'. It behaves like a lattice of compact or regular-closed pieces of a space, studied point-free.

On p.111 he stated the first axiom of 'rapports' (Atomisation 1): for every figure F, the family (X⁰)_{X∈F} in Σ_A is admissible. Admissible means, roughly, generating a Boolean subalgebra in which the members are disjoint.

On this page he first observes that this axiom involves only Δ, | | and 𝓕. It does not yet involve the containment or way-below relations ˚≪ and ≪, so he decides to strengthen it.

To motivate the strengthening he works in a spatios Σ:
- He considers finite sets 𝔄 of nonempty, pairwise disjoint elements of Σ, called 'discrete' spatial figures, forming Figspatdisc(Σ) ⊂ Figspat(Σ).
- On these he defines a refinement preorder: 𝔅 ≪ 𝔄 iff every b ∈ 𝔅 lies below some a ∈ 𝔄. This is the lower (Hoare) preorder restricted to finite antichains of disjoint pieces, and he notes it is induced by ≪ on Figspat.
- For a ∈ 𝔄 he sets 𝔅_a = {b ∈ 𝔅 : b ≤ a}, a' = Sup 𝔅_a ≤ a, and a'' = a ∧ ∁a' (the 'remainder' of a not covered by the pieces of 𝔅 inside it).

The next page (Lemma 2) uses these to characterize when 𝔄 ∪ 𝔅 lies in a Boolean subalgebra Σ' of Σ (stable under Sup, Inf, ∁). The criterion is that a = a' ∨ a'' for all a, and that 𝔅̂ = 𝔅 ∪ {a'' ≠ 0} is admissible. The Boolean algebra generated by 𝔅̂ is then the smallest such Σ'.

This leads to a strengthened axiom At-0-VV²: for F ≪ G in the magasin, the pair {A, B} of underlying elements must be admissible. The purpose is a combinatorial-lattice foundation for 'spaces of figures', apparently in the spirit of a point-free or tame topology.
errors: The last line as written reads a'' = b ∧ ∁b'. It is clearly a slip for a'' = a ∧ ∁a', which is the definition used in Lemma 2 on the next page.

In a genuine Boolean algebra a = a' ∨ (a ∧ ∁a') is automatic. Condition (ii)a of Lemma 2 is only meaningful because ∁ in a spatios is not assumed to be a Boolean complement (e.g. a closure-of-complement operation). The page does not make this explicit.

ideas.what: Observation that the axiom of 'rapports' involves only Δ, | | and 𝓕, not the order relations ≪ or ˚≪, and the decision to strengthen it so that it does
ideas.modern_name: compatibility axiom between a coverage/figure structure and a refinement order

ideas.what: Discrete spatial figures: finite sets of nonempty pairwise disjoint elements of a spatios, with the refinement preorder 𝔅 ≪ 𝔄 iff every b lies below some a
ideas.modern_name: finite antichains / partitions with the lower (Hoare) preorder; refinement of disjoint families
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (domain theory, Hoare powerdomain; classical partition refinement)

ideas.what: Decomposition of a into the covered part a' = Sup 𝔅_a and the remainder a'' = a ∧ ∁a', used to test whether 𝔄 ∪ 𝔅 lies in a Boolean subalgebra
ideas.modern_name: common Boolean refinement / generated Boolean subalgebra in a lattice with (non-Boolean) complementation, e.g. regular closed sets

missed.claim: The page is part of Grothendieck's otherwise unpublished 1986 axiomatics of 'spatios' / 'ateliers' / 'magasins'. This is a point-free, Boolean-lattice-based foundation for spatial figures, and its existence and structure are largely absent from the secondary literature. This particular page, however, contains only routine definitions.
missed.quote: L'axiome des rapports ne concerne directement que les données Δ, | | et 𝓕 ⊂ 𝔓(𝒜) sur 𝒜, et ne fait pas intervenir encore ˚≪ ou ≪. Je conviens de le renforcer ainsi.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents a late Grothendieck attempt at foundations of (tame / point-free) topology via lattices of pieces. This could be compared with locale theory, o-minimal cell structures and mereotopology, but this page alone is preliminary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lattice-theoretic setup (refinement of disjoint finite families, generated Boolean subalgebra) inside an unpublished axiomatics. The program itself is little known, but nothing on this page is a new result.
transcription_corrections: Last line: the image reads approximately "a'' = b ∧ ∁b'"; the intended meaning is a'' = a ∧ ∁a'.
"non [?] compacts [-non-] vides": the image suggests a struck-through word followed by "non vides mutuellement disjointes", i.e. 'parties non vides mutuellement disjointes'. 'compacts' is uncertain.
"les voilà nommées discrètes" is uncertain; it is probably 'que nous appellerons discrètes (disc.)' or similar.
𝔄, 𝔅 are written as hollow/barred capitals (A, B with strokes), not plain A, B.
The marginal '117' is the archive page number; '112' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination.
